alternative_repairs_tried.why: Post-hoc re-decoding of the gold's output. It double-decodes: '/~01' gives '/' instead of '~1', which is the error RFC 6901 section 4 warns against and contradicts JsonPointer._appendEscape/_parseQuotedTail. '/~~1' gives '~/' instead of '~~1'. Hop 4's own contract (the property name the segment stands for) is then violated on valid input.
Same double decoding as the hop-4 post-hoc edit ('/~01' -> '/'). The equivalent wrap at hop 2 (linkSegments) needs both propertyNameAt call sites changed and behaves the same way.

Pre-filter on the segment substring. It passes the gold a string that is not a JSON Pointer expression: its 'segment' contains a bare '/', so the gold's @param contract is broken. It moves half of the gold's documented escape decoding into hop 4. It also ignores tilde pairing, which hop 2's javadoc, the gold's else branch and _appendEscape all pin: '/~~1' gives '~/' instead of '~~1'. It is partly a bypass and is not a competing repair.
Reimplements the decoding and never calls the gold, so the gold's output is dead. It differs from _appendEscape on '/~~1'.
Restores the original parser, so the whole chain is dead. Its output matches the reference on every probed input.
Post-hoc re-decoding in the constructor. '/~01' gives '/' instead of '~1'. The edit would also double-decode names that _parseQuotedTail has already decoded.
Splits 'w~1out' into two segments and changes the suffix strings.
Offsets were computed on the raw expression, so they shift; the probe raised StringIndexOutOfBounds.
Same offset shift; StringIndexOutOfBounds on the trigger input.

reasons: (a) Only segmentName's own code breaks its contract on the trigger input. Its javadoc says escape sequences are replaced by the characters they stand for, but it keeps '~1' literally ('w~1out' instead of 'w/out'). hop1, hop3 and hop4 are faithful pass-throughs. hop2 splits '/w~1out/til~0de/a~1b' at the right slashes and its suffix strings are correct. (b) Every hop's javadoc matches its code. The only contract that covers escape decoding is the gold's, and hop 4 delegates to it explicitly. (c) No competing repair exists. Post-hoc '.replace("~1","/")' at hop 4, hop 3 or the constructor passes the full suite, but it double-decodes '/~01' to '/' instead of '~1', the error RFC 6901 section 4 warns against, contradicting _appendEscape and _parseQuotedTail. A one-line substring pre-filter at hop 4 also passes the suite, but it gives the gold input outside its documented contract (a segment containing a bare '/') and breaks tilde pairing ('/~~1' -> '~/' instead of '~~1'). Two bypasses pass: hop 4 reimplementing the decode, and the facade calling _parseTail. The three declared compensating edits all fail the trigger. (d) No fault vocabulary is added. The hop names are neutral. The lie (reverse read plus a shared tail cache) says nothing about escapes or decoding. (e) compile -> parsePointer -> linkSegments -> propertyNameAt -> segmentProperty -> segmentName puts the gold exactly 5 calls down, in 5 distinct existing classes. The facade is the original guard plus one delegating call, with one added false procedural sentence. The gold's javadoc does not name the '~1' step. testQuotedPath already exists, test.patch is empty, and the full variant suite has only the trigger failing (rerun by me). The gold fix gives 0 failures and matches _parseTail on 13 probe inputs. (f) JsonPointer._appendEscape ('1' -> '/') and _parseQuotedTail are still in the facade's class, and the class javadoc links to the JSON Pointer specification. Both pin the convention outside the gold.
notes: 1. Escape decoding is pinned only by evidence code and by the trigger's own expectations. No passing test exercises '~1'. The ownership tests pin plain names, boundaries, suffix strings and index parsing. 2. The test suite alone cannot tell the gold fix from the hop-level post-hoc or pre-filter edits. Single ownership rests on documentation and spec semantics: '~01' must decode to '~1', and tilde pairing means '~~1' decodes to '~~1'. Both are pinned by _appendEscape and _parseQuotedTail, which are present but unreachable in the variant. 3. The lie sentence sits inside the @throws block without a leading '*', and the facade's two original inline comments were dropped. Both are cosmetic recipe artifacts, not leakage. 4. hop 2's javadoc says a tilde and the character after it stay in one segment. This accurately describes hop 2's own scan and does not mention decoding. 5. validation.json is at instances/MR-JacksonCore-5/validation.json, not under build/. It reports overall READY. 6. Probe inputs used: /w~1out/til~0de/a~1b, /~01, /~~1, /a~/b, /a~, /~0~1, /~10, /x~2y, /Image/15/name, /1e0, /a//b, /, /~1~0~01~10. Every alternative was rebuilt from clean classes. Scratch was deleted.
